findings.title: Logging annotation cleanup counts at Error level
findings.body: In CleanAnnotations and CleanOrphanedAnnotationTags, r.log.Error(...) is used to log routine/successful cleanup progress (e.g. "Annotations to clean by time", "cleaned annotations by time"), not actual errors. This will pollute error logs/alerts with normal operational information and could trigger false error-rate alarms.

findings.title: Fetch-then-delete by ID introduces TOCTOU window per batch
findings.body: CleanAnnotations/CleanOrphanedAnnotationTags now fetch IDs in one query/transaction and delete them in a separate one. Between fetch and delete, the row's state could change (e.g., it stops matching the original criteria, or in rare cases is already deleted by another process), making the delete silently delete fewer or different rows than counted, and the reported 'affected' count can diverge from fetched IDs count without any error surfaced. This is called out as acceptable in the comment for under-deletion, but there's no safeguard or logging distinguishing fetched vs. actually deleted counts (the Error logs intermix len(ids) and x without clarifying whether they match), making root-causing data-mismatch issues difficult in production.

findings.title: SQLite ID interpolation uses unparameterized values but non-SQLite path still bounded by driver parameter limits
findings.body: deleteByIDs falls back to raw string interpolation of IDs only for SQLite over the parameter limit; for other DB types (e.g., MySQL/Postgres) all IDs are passed as query parameters regardless of batch size. If AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize is configured very large for MySQL/Postgres, this could exceed those drivers' parameter count limits (MySQL's limit is typically 65535 placeholders), causing a runtime failure that isn't tested or guarded against for non-SQLite databases.

findings.title: Cleanup job interval reduced from 10 minutes to 1 minute without justification
findings.body: The ticker interval for background cleanup jobs (including snapshot/version/short-url/query-history cleanup, not just annotations) was changed from every 10 minutes to every 1 minute. This 10x increase in cleanup job frequency affects all cleanup jobs system-wide, not just annotation cleanup cited in the PR description, and could increase DB load significantly. There's no mention of this tradeoff in the PR description, and it isn't scoped only to annotation cleanup.
